faq.q: Why is sharing raw HAR files dangerous?
faq.a: HTTP Archive files contain complete records of web browser network activity, including session cookies, JWT authentication tokens, OAuth authorization headers, and personal form POST payloads. Sharing unscrubbed HAR files allows recipients to hijack your active account sessions.

faq.q: Which sensitive fields does this tool sanitize?
faq.a: The tool systematically purges Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and custom API token headers, along with query parameters containing keywords such as token, secret, password, key, or apikey.

faq.q: Does sanitization break the network timing data needed by support?
faq.a: No. Request methods, URLs, response status codes, timing metrics (DNS, SSL, TTFB, download), and header structures remain intact so technical teams can effectively diagnose latency and network errors.

faq.q: Are my HAR logs uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. The entire JSON parsing and string redaction pipeline executes locally inside your browser memory. Your network captures are never transmitted across the network.

articleHtml:
HTTP Archive (HAR) Security and Credential Exposure

HTTP Archive (HAR) files are standardized JSON-formatted logs captured by web browser Developer Tools to record client-server HTTP communications. While essential for troubleshooting content delivery networks (CDNs), API error responses, and web application latency, unredacted HAR files are hazardous security vectors.

Whenever a support engineer requests a HAR file to diagnose a billing glitch or user interface bug, the captured file inherently records every single HTTP request header transmitted during that session. This includes active Cookie headers, Set-Cookie directives, and Authorization: Bearer [JWT] tokens. If shared through email, ticketing systems, or public message boards, third parties can immediately replay these tokens to impersonate your session.

Redaction Protocol Specifications

  • Session Cookie Erasure: All Cookie and Set-Cookie array structures are cleared, preventing session token theft.
  • Bearer Token Neutralization: Values corresponding to Authorization, X-Auth-Token, and Proxy-Authorization are replaced with static redaction masks.
  • Query String Token Filtering: Parameters containing sensitive substrings (e.g., api_key, access_token, token, secret) have values sanitized while preserving URL routing.
  • Network Timing Preservation: DNS lookup times, TCP connection latencies, TLS negotiation durations, and response body status codes remain intact for diagnostic utility.

Local Sandbox Execution Guarantee

Uploading an unredacted HAR file to an online cloud converter defeats the purpose of redaction. Toolkit Gen operates strictly within local browser memory via JavaScript JSON stream manipulation. Your confidential logs, API keys, and corporate session tokens are sanitized on your device before network sharing.

Anatomy of an HTTP Archive and Sensitive Data Vectors

The HTTP Archive (HAR) specification, maintained by the W3C Web Performance Working Group, defines a comprehensive JSON schema for recording web browser network interactions. Whenever a developer opens Developer Tools and exports a HAR file, the browser serializes the complete state of every HTTP transaction initiated by the current session.

While invaluable for diagnosing latency bottlenecks, caching misconfigurations, and REST API failures, raw HAR files represent severe credential compromise hazards. Modern Single Page Applications (SPAs) and cloud architectures transmit sensitive bearer tokens and session identifiers across virtually every API request. If an engineer shares an unredacted HAR file in a public GitHub issue or third-party vendor support ticket, active user sessions can be hijacked instantly.

Redaction Categories and Security Scope

  • Authentication Headers: Scans and replaces values for Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, X-Auth-Token, X-Api-Key, and Bearer tokens with sanitized placeholder masks.
  • Cookie Reservoirs: Strips all entries from both request.cookies and response.cookies arrays, as well as redacting raw Cookie and Set-Cookie header strings.
  • Query String Token Redaction: Inspects URL query strings and scrubs parameter values containing sensitive substrings such as token, api_key, secret, or password.
  • Diagnostic Preservation: Preserves request methods, URLs, status codes, response headers, and exact timing breakdown metrics (DNS, Connect, SSL, Send, Wait, Receive) so support teams can resolve technical issues.

Client-Side Sanitization Pipeline Standards

Uploading an unredacted HAR file to a remote cloud conversion service directly violates data governance protocols (including SOC 2, HIPAA, and GDPR). Toolkit Gen parses, filters, and re-serializes your HAR JSON files entirely in your browser's local JavaScript memory. Your session cookies, passwords, and private API credentials never leave your personal computer.
